comment: The qualified-name forms, BOTH of them. `expression-shapes.icl` pins the ALIAS form (`M.lookupOne`), and it was the lane's only qualified-name coverage until now. Measured over the 320-file Clean universe, the pinned grammar emits `qualified_identifier` — the node that alias form desugars to — exactly TWICE, and both sites are this repository's own fixtures. The form real Clean code uses is `single_quoted_name`: 233 corpus sites, 87 of them in application-head position, and the pre-round analyzer named the node type NOWHERE. So the lane's only test exercised a form no Clean codebase contains and the form every Clean codebase uses had no test. This fixture is the corpus form, taken from eastwood/src/linter/EastwoodLint.icl. The two bugs this fixture pins are both real and both were found by writing it: (1) the quote in a Clean qualified name wraps the MODULE, not the whole name — the corpus spells `'Data.Error'.Ok`, and a normalizer that removed one leading `'` and required one trailing `'` returned null for all 78 corpus heads while the branch looked live; (2) a qualified name in TYPE position is a different node entirely (`single_quoted_name` under `strict_type`/`type_application`, 39 corpus sites) and needs its own case in the type-reference reader.

expectRelationships.comment: THE corpus form. The source spells `'Data.Error'.Ok`; the target is the same name with its quote characters dropped, so the target is the name a symbol in the imported file would carry. The qualifier `Data.Error` is recorded in the edge metadata rather than being re-parsed out of the target.  TIER: `reference_qualified` — the `'Data.Error'.Ok` spelling, quote-stripped: the target is identified by the source's own qualified reference, and `Data.Error` is not declared here
three qualified calls in one expression, each a separate edge on its own line

A qualified TYPE in signature position. It is a `single_quoted_name` under the result type — a different node from the expression-position one and a different code path — and without its own case in the type-reference reader the reference was lost. 39 corpus sites (`strict_type` 24, `type_application` 9, `type_function` 6, `question_type` 3, `list_type` 2).

CHANGED: the SELECTIVE import item list. `from Data.Error import instance Functor (MaybeError a)` names exactly one thing, and the edge says `Data.Error:Functor` — the `<module>:<item>` form src/ast/import-resolution.ts joins against the exporting file's export surface. Before this round every import edge was `<module>:*`, which is the form that can never resolve. 943 items over 367 corpus imports reached nothing.
a whole-module import takes the wildcard, which the resolver documents as legitimately unresolved: a namespace has no single target symbol

`cfg.diagnostic` is a record field read and the field is declared by this file  TIER: `structural` — a record field this file declares, read through a `field_access` — structural, and in-file by construction (the lane emits no `uses` edge to a field it cannot prove)

forbidRelationships.comment: the quote characters are dropped: the target is the name the imported file's symbol carries, not the source's spelling
the module part of a qualified name is not itself a type reference — the whole qualified name is

a qualified CONSTRUCTOR in body position is a construction, not a call. This file does not declare `Ok` (it imports it), and the lane's rule is that an uppercase applied name no declaration in this file explains emits NO edge — measured, only 19.3% of that population is a data constructor and the rest are Clean uppercase FUNCTIONS, macros and types. So the correct reading of `'Data.Error'.Ok msg` in a single file is silence, and the `calls` row above is about the FUNCTION position, not this one.
the receiver is a value, not a field
an imported symbol is never contained by the importing module

expectImports.comment: `import qualified Data.Error` — a whole-module qualified import: isQualified lives in the import's METADATA, and its item list is empty, so the wildcard edge is the record

`from Data.Error import instance Functor (MaybeError a)` — the SELECTIVE item list. Before this round every import carried `items: []`, which is the 943-item hole the `<module>:<item>` edge is written for.

expectReturnType.comment: the RESULT type keeps the module qualification the source spells, because the qualified name is the type's identity

expectQualifiedCalls.comment: the `qualified_calls` COLUMN carries the same fact as the edges, for product search. It was empty for every Clean symbol in existence before this round because no Clean symbol emitted a qualified call.
